title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evaluation results against the agreed prompt sets and scoring rubric. Discussed regressions on multi-step workflows, tuning suggestions (few-shot prompts, guardrails), and action items for next benchmark run. Agreed to run a focused canary on high-risk intents and share updated spreadsheets and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call and we'll jump into the eval sheet.
[00:10] Priya (Atlas): Hey, Priya here. Evan and Tara are with me.
[00:15] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos here. Good to see you all.
[00:22] Maya: We circulated the weekly eval spreadsheet, link in chat (Eval spreadsheet: https://redwood.share/eval-atlas-v1). Does everyone have it?
[00:28] Evan: Yep, got it.
[00:30] Priya: Yep, open. Thanks.
[00:33] Carlos: Cool. Quick TL;DR — overall pass rate is 87% down from 92% baseline last week on the full prompt set. The main drops are in the multi-step reconciliation prompts and a few edge-case entity normalizations.
[00:50] Priya: That's the thing — multi-step flows are customer visible so it's a blocker if we don't tighten that. Any idea what's triggering the regression?
[01:00] Carlos: We dug into logs. Two things: (1) model variant A (Redwood-Opti-v1) had more hallucinations on long context, likely caching/k-v cache mismatch — sometimes the k-v cash isn't reloaded after branch prompts; (2) a prompt change on the system prompt where a stray word was added in the engineering branch.
[01:20] Tara: Wait, k-v cash? you mean KV cache? the transcription in the doc calls it k-v cash, haha.
[01:25] Maya: yes, KV cache. Sorry about the typo in the doc.
[01:28] Evan: How bad are hallucinations? numbers?
[01:32] Carlos: Measured hallucination triggers at ~3.5% on affected intents vs target <2%. Latency also crept by ~15% for those flows due to larger prefix lengths — average P95 increased from 420ms to 480ms. Token cost per request up ~8%.
[01:50] Priya: Ok that explains user-facing flakiness. Any quick mitigation we can apply?
[01:55] Carlos: A few quick wins: restore the previous system prompt for the canary, introduce a short 2-shot example for the reconciliation flow, and enable prefix KV preloading for sessions flagged as multi-step. Those are config changes, low risk.
[02:10] Maya: We should also add a guardrail rule to detect soft hallucination patterns we saw — a regex-based verifier for entity IDs + a fallback to ask for clarification instead of inventing.
[02:22] Priya: That would help. We're also worried about wrong PII redaction steps — one case slipped through.
[02:28] Carlos: Right — for PII we recommend the redwood built-in scrubber with customer regex overrides. We can push a rule to the staging canary.
[02:36] Evan: On scoring, are we confident the rubric is stable? I noticed some borderline cases flagged differently week over week.
[02:42] Maya: Good call. The rubric uses three labels: Correct, Partial, Incorrect, plus Safety flag. We saw annotator drift on Partial vs Correct. Suggestion: add a short calibration set of 25 golden prompts and re-run human review with new instructions.
[02:58] Priya: Can you add those examples? We'll have our data team re-annotate.
[03:02] Maya: Yes — we'll add calibration examples to the spreadsheet.
[03:06] Tara: One other question — does the regression look like model drift or config change?
[03:11] Carlos: Mixed signals. The system prompt change correlates with some failures; but remote traces indicate a quantization kernel selection difference when moving between infra nodes — that explains the latency bump. It's rare but reproducible on our dedicated GPU pool.
[03:24] Priya: So it's both infra and prompt.
[03:26] Carlos: Correct. We'll run a controlled canary: deploy system prompt rollback + KV preload on a subset of traffic routed to Redwood-Opti-v1 in us-east-1.
[03:36] Evan: Timeline?
[03:39] Maya: Proposed: Carlos to run tune & canary by Friday 2025-06-20, share results Monday. We'll also re-run the eval spreadsheet with the 2-shot variants.
[03:49] Priya: Sounds good. Regarding security docs — we still need SOC2 scoping info for our compliance team.
[03:55] Maya: I'll send the SOC2 summary and audit contact by Thursday 2025-06-19.
[04:00] Tara: And about the dataset — we found 12 prompts that consistently trigger hallucination; we'll paste them in the sheet today.
[04:07] Carlos: Great. We'll add targeted unit tests for those prompts so regression alerts will fire if we slip below the pass threshold.
[04:12] Evan: What's the pass threshold again?
[04:15] Maya: For this POC success criteria we agreed on >=90% Correct or Partial (with under 2% hallucination) on priority intents.
[04:23] Priya: Right. Current 87% is under that.
[04:26] Maya: Action plan recap coming up. Any other blockers?
[04:30] Tara: Not from data infra side. We'll provide the edge-case list.
[04:33] Priya: Can we also get a short doc on guardrail tuning? Our security team wants to understand failure modes.
[04:38] Carlos: We'll share a short runbook and example rules.
[04:42] Maya: Ok, I'll capture next steps.
[04:45] [recap by Maya] Maya: Action items: Carlos will run the canary with system prompt rollback + KV preload and two-shot prompt variant; deliver results by 2025-06-20. Maya will share SOC2 summary and the calibration set by 2025-06-19. Priya/Tara will paste edge-case prompts and re-annotate calibration set by 2025-06-18. We'll add regression unit tests and guardrail runbook to staging. Next sync same time next week unless earlier needed.
[05:10] Evan: Thanks all.
[05:12] Priya: Thanks.
[05:14] Maya: Thanks everyone, bye.
